heading: ## Purpose
reason: Conformance: asserts THIS repo ships the three Codex-runtime mechanics the Purpose section names — the eight thin SKILL.md bindings, the plugin hook bundle (hooks.json + footgun guard), and the structural gate (now shipped from livespec_dev_tooling.driver_checks.plugin_structure; the spec's literal dev-tooling/check_plugin_structure.py path is stale drift). Control-armed: a missing binding, hooks.json, guard, or gate module fails.

heading: ## Scope boundary
reason: RESIDUAL (meta): governs what the Driver spec owns vs. what is core-owned/out-of-scope, plus the upstream-wins rule. No mechanical check enforces a scoping declaration and it names no runtime behavior. Recommend spec-restructure or accept as permanent meta residual.

heading: ## Terminology
reason: RESIDUAL (glossary): defines Driver / core-root / Binding / Thin-transport binding, deferring the family vocabulary upstream. Pure glossary — no enforcing check, no runtime behavior.

heading: ## Public surface
reason: The Driver's public surface is the eight livespec:* skill bindings; the e2e harness asserts the discovered skill set equals exactly those eight, so this heading is witnessed by the same integration test.

heading: ## Lifecycle and evolution
reason: RESIDUAL (core-doctor governance): the SPECIFICATION tree evolves through the livespec loop; the history/vNNN structure is enforced against this repo by core doctor-static (check-doctor-static in the aggregate), whose runner ships in the livespec CORE plugin — not importable in-process here, and subprocess is banned in tests — so it cannot be re-bound to a pytest conformance test. Same blocker as the git-jsonl lifecycle rows; maintainer disposition: heading->check_id mapping, or make core doctor checks importable.

heading: ## Plugin manifest and marketplace
reason: The Codex manifest and marketplace catalog must agree (plugin.json is the source of truth); this control-armed test asserts the structural check convicts a drifted marketplace/plugin.json description.

heading: ## Skill-binding set
reason: The binding set is exactly the eight EXPECTED_SKILLS; this control-armed test asserts the structural check convicts both a missing and an extra skill directory, enforcing the set is neither short nor over.

heading: ## Core-root resolution
reason: Conformance: runs the plugin-structure check-runner against THIS repo (the pristine tree passing is the control arm, proving every binding carries the ordered resolution's `codex plugin list --json -m livespec` invocation) and against a fixture binding with the snippet stripped (reddens).

heading: ## Fenced-invocation discipline
reason: Fenced wrapper invocations MUST resolve via $LIVESPEC_CORE_ROOT and MUST NOT use 'uv run'; this control-armed test asserts the structural check convicts a fenced 'uv run' wrapper line.

heading: ## Hook bundle
reason: The shipped hook bundle MUST include livespec/hooks/livespec_footgun_guard.py wired into hooks.json; this control-armed test asserts the structural check convicts a bundle missing the guard script.

heading: ## Versioning
reason: Conformance: runs the plugin-structure check-runner against THIS repo (pristine tree passes — control arm) and against a fixture whose plugin.json version is blanked (reddens), realizing plugin.json.version as the single non-empty source of truth.

heading: ## Inherited from livespec
reason: RESIDUAL (meta/inherited): declares that every applicable livespec-core constraint applies unmodified with upstream-wins. The concrete constraints are enforced in their owning repos; this heading adds no this-repo-checkable rule of its own.

heading: ## Binding constraints
reason: Codex binding bodies MUST NOT carry Claude-Driver markers; this control-armed test asserts the structural check convicts a body carrying the 'Claude Code Driver' phrase.

heading: ## Resolution-substrate constraints
reason: Conformance: runs the plugin-structure check-runner against THIS repo (pristine tree passes — control arm) and against a fixture binding that reaches core scripts via the Driver's own plugin-root placeholder (reddens), realizing the resolution-substrate rule that a binding MUST NOT short-circuit to the Driver root, which has no scripts/.

heading: ## Structural-check constraints
reason: Witnesses that the shipped Codex plugin tree satisfies the whole structural gate (codex_profile_violations returns no violations); the sibling rejection tests in the same module witness that each constrained defect is convicted.

heading: ## Forbidden patterns
reason: The forbidden patterns enumerated here (uv run / literal .claude-plugin path / Driver plugin-root placeholder in a fenced wrapper; /livespec: slash form, installed_plugins.json, 'Claude Code Driver', livespec-driver-claude in a binding body; extra/missing skill dir; hooks.json top-level description) are exactly what the structural check convicts. This test asserts the shipped tree carries none of them; the sibling rejection tests in the same module (test_structural_check_rejects_*) each witness that the corresponding forbidden pattern is detected.

heading: ## Factory routing
reason: Witnesses the committed-config half of this heading directly: dispatcher.factories carries exactly one entry, petri, declaring "registry": true with no server and no docker_host value, so no committed factory entry names a machine. The sibling test_factory_routing_default_factory_names_petri in the same module witnesses the dispatcher.default_factory requirement. The resolution half — that a dispatch resolves petri by name from the dispatching host's rendered /etc/livespec/fabro-factories.json — is host-captured by livespec-driver-codex-extptf, since no factory sandbox can read the control node's registry; this entry retires the RESIDUAL TODO that livespec-driver-codex-cea owned until a conformance test replaced it.

heading: ## Boundary
reason: RESIDUAL (meta): scopes what this NFR file covers vs. contracts.md / constraints.md. Descriptive boundary statement — no enforcing check, no runtime behavior.

heading: ## Inherited from livespec
reason: RESIDUAL (meta/inherited): the family-standard operational disciplines (primary-checkout commit-refuse hook, toolchain pinning) are owned and enforced upstream; this heading restates inheritance, not a this-repo-checkable rule. (The primary-checkout refusal's Driver-side fast-guard IS witnessed via the footgun scenario row.)

heading: ## Task-runner discipline
reason: lefthook.yml and CI YAML MUST route dev-tool calls through 'just <target>'; this control-armed test asserts check-no-direct-tool-invocation passes on this repo and convicts a fabricated lefthook hook shelling out to pytest directly.

heading: ## Repo layout
reason: Conformance: asserts every path the Repo-layout table declares exists in THIS repo (marketplace, plugin manifest, skills, hook bundle, dev-tooling reconciler/observer, the three test surfaces, spec tree, toolchain config). Control-armed: a missing declared path fails.

heading: ## Enforcement suite
reason: Conformance: asserts every gate the Enforcement-suite section names (check-plugin-structure, check-hooks, check-e2e-cli, check-codex-skill-picker, check-dev-tooling, check-heading-coverage, check-lint, check-format) is a recipe in the justfile. Control-armed: a renamed or dropped gate fails.

heading: ## Build and release
reason: Conformance: asserts THIS repo's plugin.json.version is non-empty (release-please-managed single source of truth) and marketplace.json carries no version field. Control-armed: an empty plugin version or a marketplace version key fails.

heading: ## Test discipline
reason: Conformance: asserts the three test surfaces the section names (tests/e2e-cli, tests/hooks, tests/dev-tooling) exist and each holds at least one test module. Control-armed: an emptied or missing surface fails.

heading: ## Spec evolution
reason: Conformance: runs the heading-coverage check-runner against THIS repo (clean, exit 0) and against a fixture spec tree with an uncovered heading (reddens, exit 1) — the mechanical teeth the Spec-evolution section names for keeping the H2 set in lockstep with the registry.

heading: ## Scenario: core-root resolution via operator override

reason: Integration-tier: injects a fenced wrapper line using the Driver's own plugin-root placeholder into the shipped tree and asserts the structural check convicts it; the pristine-copy pass is the control arm.

reason: Integration-tier: removes one of the eight skill dirs and adds an unexpected one, asserting both the missing- and unexpected-directory violations fire against the otherwise-clean shipped tree.

heading: ## Scenario: marketplace description drift is rejected
reason: Integration-tier: drifts the plugin.json description from the marketplace catalog and asserts the structural check convicts the mismatch; plugin.json is the source of truth.

heading: ## Scenario: footgun guard denies a never-legitimate command
reason: Integration-tier (tests.integration allowlisted): drives the plugin-shipped PreToolUse footgun guard via its hook I/O contract and asserts a never-legitimate command (git commit --no-verify) yields a 'deny' decision naming --no-verify.

heading: ## Scenario: auto-memory guard refuses every write route into an agent memory directory
reason: Integration-tier (tests.integration allowlisted): drives the plugin-shipped auto-memory guard via its hook I/O contract and asserts every write route (Write, Edit, apply_patch, shell redirect/tee/sed -i/cp/inline python) into either memory directory yields one identical 'deny' reason naming AGENTS.md and .ai/<topic>.md; a sibling test asserts reads and rm pass.

heading: ## Scenario: footgun guard fails open on the dangerous string as data
reason: Integration-tier: parametrized over the dangerous string as DATA (echo, git config --get read) plus empty / non-JSON / non-Bash stdin, asserting the guard emits no deny decision and exits 0 (fail-open).

heading: ## Scenario: commit at the primary checkout is refused
reason: Integration-tier: drives the plugin-shipped PreToolUse footgun guard exactly as Codex runs it (hook-input JSON on stdin) against a hermetic primary checkout (a repo whose livespec.primaryPath equals its own root); the guard DENIES the file-write and names the worktree alternative. The sibling fail-open suite is the control arm.

heading: ## Scenario: long-running hooks survive a Driver cache update
reason: Integration-tier host-aware acceptance driven over the REAL installed Driver payload: it copies the host's actual current cache payload to a scratch CODEX_HOME, runs the real observer while that payload is replaced the way Codex replaces one (successor written incrementally, old version directory removed), and asserts latest does not move while the successor is half-written, then that the hook paths captured under the retired version still resolve, in one hop through latest, to scripts of the validated current payload. Deliberately narrowed — it does not publish a Driver release to make the marketplace advance, because that would couple the suite to the release pipeline; every step downstream of the release is exercised. The amended scenario's trust assertion (Codex trusts the Driver's hooks, and any trust the Driver re-established followed verification of its hook definitions and entrypoints against the release tag) is not yet exercised by this test; the integration-tier test for it is owed by livespec-driver-codex-v52m6a.
